In [16]:
data = "This Product is GREAT but  I amn't liking the colors as I am thinking they are WORST"
# 1. convert into lowercase
data = data.lower()
print("1. lowercase:",data)

# 2. tokenize
data1 = data.split()
print("2. Words using split:\n",data1)
data2 = word_tokenize(data)
print("2. Words using tokenize:\n",data2)

#3. removal of stop words
nltk_stopwords = set(stopwords.words("english"))
#print("English stopwords: ",nltk_stopwords)

for w in data2:
    if w in nltk_stopwords:
        count_w = data2.count(w)
        for words in range(count_w):
            data2.remove(w)
print("3. Words after Removal of stop words:\n",data2)

#4 Stemming: changing the word to its root form
stemm = PorterStemmer()
data3 = [stemm.stem(word) for word in data2]
print("Text after stemming:\n",data3)

# 4 POS Tagging
# https://stackoverflow.com/questions/15388831/what-are-all-possible-pos-tags-of-nltk
data_tag = nltk.pos_tag(data3)
print("After POS Tagging:\n",data_tag)

#Lemmetizer
lemm = WordNetLemmatizer()
data_lemm = [lemm.lemmatize(word) for word in data3]
print("After Lemmatizing:\n",data_lemm)

1. lowercase: this product is great but  i amn't liking the colors as i am thinking they are worst
2. Words using split:
 ['this', 'product', 'is', 'great', 'but', 'i', "amn't", 'liking', 'the', 'colors', 'as', 'i', 'am', 'thinking', 'they', 'are', 'worst']
2. Words using tokenize:
 ['this', 'product', 'is', 'great', 'but', 'i', 'am', "n't", 'liking', 'the', 'colors', 'as', 'i', 'am', 'thinking', 'they', 'are', 'worst']
3. Words after Removal of stop words:
 ['product', 'great', 'i', "n't", 'liking', 'colors', 'i', 'thinking', 'are', 'worst']
Text after stemming:
 ['product', 'great', 'i', "n't", 'like', 'color', 'i', 'think', 'are', 'worst']
After POS Tagging:
 [('product', 'NN'), ('great', 'JJ'), ('i', 'VBP'), ("n't", 'RB'), ('like', 'IN'), ('color', 'NN'), ('i', 'NN'), ('think', 'VBP'), ('are', 'VBP'), ('worst', 'JJS')]
After Lemmatizing:
 ['product', 'great', 'i', "n't", 'like', 'color', 'i', 'think', 'are', 'worst']

class="ArticleHeader_main_wrapper__yCL1Y" style="display:flex;align-items:center"><div style="width:100%"><div class="ArticleHeader_article-title__futDC"><h1>POS(Parts-Of-Speech) Tagging in NLP</h1></div><div class="ArticleHeader_last_updated_parent__ohhpb"><div class="ArticleHeader_last_updated_parent--top_row__cg1JG"><div class="ArticleHeader_last_updated_parent--date__O011V"><span>Last Updated : </span><span>2 Jul, 2026</span></div><div class="ArticleHeader_last_updated_parent--three_dot_dropdown__yslcL"><div styles="[object Object]"><div class="ArticleThreeDot_threedotcontainer__dfGWD"><div class="ArticleThreeDot_comment__gJfFl" style="background-position:0px 0px"></div><div class="ArticleThreeDot_improve___NFbl" style="background-position:-40px -521px"></div><div class="ArticleThreeDot_threedot-wrapper__q4ELY"><ul class="ArticleThreeDot_threedot__ZQ19q"><li></li><li></li><li></li></ul></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="MainArticleContent_articleMainContentCss__b_1_R article--viewer_content"><div class="a-wrapper"><div class="content"><div class="text"><div class="html-chunk"><p dir="ltr"><span>Parts of Speech (PoS) tagging is a fundamental task in Natural Language Processing (NLP) where each word in a sentence is assigned a grammatical category such as noun, verb, adjective or adverb. </span></p><ul><li value="1"><span>This process help machines to understand the structure and meaning of sentences by identifying the roles of words and their relationships.</span></li><li value="2"><span>Analyzes the context of words to determine their correct part of speech</span></li><li value="3"><span>Improves text analysis, parsing, machine translation, and information extraction</span></li><li value="4"><span>Widely used in text classification, sentiment analysis, chatbots, and search engine</span></li></ul><gfg-carousel><gfg-carousel-content alt="a_quick_brown_fox_jumps_over_a_lazy_dog.webp" height="400" src="https://media.geeksforgeeks.org/wp-content/uploads/20250819114114256836/a_quick_brown_fox_jumps_over_a_lazy_dog.webp" width="800"></gfg-carousel-content><gfg-carousel-content alt="architecture_of_pos_tagging.webp" height="400" src="https://media.geeksforgeeks.org/wp-content/uploads/20250819114113512745/architecture_of_pos_tagging.webp" width="800"></gfg-carousel-content><gfg-carousel-content alt="types_of_pos_tagging_.webp" height="400" src="https://media.geeksforgeeks.org/wp-content/uploads/20250819114112908101/types_of_pos_tagging_.webp" width="800"></gfg-carousel-content><gfg-carousel-content alt="applications_of_pos_tagging.webp" height="400" src="https://media.geeksforgeeks.org/wp-content/uploads/20250819114113932684/applications_of_pos_tagging.webp" width="800"></gfg-carousel-content><gfg-carousel-content alt="challenges_of_pos_tagging.webp" height="400" src="https://media.geeksforgeeks.org/wp-content/uploads/20250819114113277817/challenges_of_pos_tagging.webp" width="800"></gfg-carousel-content></gfg-carousel><p dir="ltr"><span>It plays an important role in various NLP applications including machine translation, sentiment analysis and information retrieval, by bridging the gap between human language and machine understanding.</span></p><h2 id="key-concepts-in-pos-tagging" style="text-align:left"><span>Key Concepts</span></h2><ol><li value="1"><b><strong>Parts of Speech</strong></b><span>: These are categories like nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, etc that define the role of a word in a sentence.</span></li><li value="2"><b><strong>Tagging</strong></b><span>: The process of assigning a specific part-of-speech label to each word in a sentence.</span></li><li value="3"><b><strong>Corpus</strong></b><span>: A large collection of text data used to train POS taggers.</span></li></ol><h3 id="example-of-pos-tagging" style="text-align:left"><span>Example of POS Tagging</span></h3><p dir="ltr"><span>Consider the sentence: "</span><b><strong>The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.</strong></b><span>"</span></p><p dir="ltr"><span>After performing POS Tagging, we get:</span></p><blockquote><ul><li value="1"><span>"The" is tagged as determiner (DT)</span></li><li value="2"><span>"quick" is tagged as adjective (JJ)</span></li><li value="3"><span>"brown" is tagged as adjective (JJ)</span></li><li value="4"><span>"fox" is tagged as noun (NN)</span></li><li value="5"><span>"jumps" is tagged as verb (VBZ)</span></li><li value="6"><span>"over" is tagged as preposition (IN)</span></li><li value="7"><span>"the" is tagged as determiner (DT)</span></li><li value="8"><span>"lazy" is tagged as adjective (JJ)</span></li><li value="9"><span>"dog" is tagged as noun (NN)</span></li></ul></blockquote><p dir="ltr"><span>Each word is assigned a tag based on its role in the sentence. For example, "quick" and "brown" are adjectives that describe the noun "fox."</span></p><h2 id="working-of-pos-tagging" style="text-align:left"><span>Working</span></h2><p dir="ltr"><span>Let\xe2\x80\x99s see various steps involved in POS tagging:</span></p><ul><li value="1"><b><strong>Tokenization</strong></b><span>: The input text is split into individual tokens (words or subwords), this step is necessary for further analysis.</span></li><li value="2"><b><strong>Preprocessing</strong></b><span>: The text is cleaned such as converting it to lowercase and removing special characters, to improve accuracy.</span></li><li value="3"><b><strong>Loading a Language Model</strong></b><span>: Tools like </span><a href="https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/python/nltk-nlp/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><span>NLTK </span></a><span>or </span><a href="https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/machine-learning/python-pos-tagging-and-lemmatization-using-spacy/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><span>SpaCy </span></a><span>use pre-trained language models to understand the grammatical rules of the language, these models have been trained on large datasets.</span></li><li value="4"><b><strong>Linguistic Analysis</strong></b><span>: The structure of the sentence is analyzed to understand the role of each word in context.</span></li><li value="5"><b><strong>POS Tagging</strong></b><span>: Each word is assigned a part-of-speech label based on its role in the sentence and the context provided by surrounding words.</span></li><li value="6"><b><strong>Evaluation</strong></b><span>: The results are checked for accuracy. If there are any errors or misclassifications, they are corrected.</span></li></ul><h2 id="types-of-pos-tagging-in-nlp" style="text-align:left"><span>Types of POS Tagging</span></h2><p dir="ltr"><span>There are different types and each has its strengths and use cases. Let\'s see few common methods:</span></p><h3 id="1-rulebased-tagging" style="text-align:left"><span>1. </span><b><strong>Rule-Based Tagging</strong></b></h3><p dir="ltr"><a href="https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/nlp/nlp-part-of-speech-default-tagging/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><span>Rule-based POS tagging</span></a><span> assigns POS tags based on predefined grammatical rules. These rules are crafted based on morphological features (like word endings) and syntactic context, making the approach highly interpretable and transparent.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;"><b><strong>Example:</strong></b></p><p dir="ltr"><b><strong>1. Rule:</strong></b><span> Assign the POS tag "Noun" to words ending in "-tion" or "-ment".</span></p><p dir="ltr"><b><strong>2. Sentence:</strong></b><span> "The presentation highlighted the key achievements of the project\'s development."</span></p><p dir="ltr"><b><strong>3. Tagged Output:</strong></b></p><ul><li value="1"><span>"presentation" \xe2\x86\x92 Noun (N)</span></li><li value="2"><span>"highlighted" \xe2\x86\x92 Verb (V)</span></li><li value="3"><span>"development" \xe2\x86\x92 Noun (N)</span></li></ul><h3 id="2-transformationbased-tagging-tbt" style="text-align:left"><span>2. </span><b><strong>Transformation-Based Tagging (TBT)</strong></b></h3><p dir="ltr"><span>TBT refines POS tags through a series of context-based transformations. Unlike statistical taggers that rely on probabilities or rule-based taggers, it starts with initial tags and improves them iteratively by applying transformation rules.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;"><b><strong>Example:</strong></b></p><ul><li value="1"><b><strong>Text:</strong></b><span> "The cat chased the mouse."</span></li><li value="2"><b><strong>Initial Tags:</strong></b><span> "The" \xe2\x80\x93 DET, "cat" \xe2\x80\x93 NOUN, "chased" \xe2\x80\x93 VERB, "the" \xe2\x80\x93 DET, "mouse" \xe2\x80\x93 NOUN</span></li><li value="3"><b><strong>Rule Applied:</strong></b><span> Change \xe2\x80\x9cchased\xe2\x80\x9d from Verb to Nounbecause it follows \xe2\x80\x9cthe\xe2\x80\x9d.</span></li><li value="4"><b><strong>Updated Tags:</strong></b><span> "chased" becomes Noun.</span></li></ul><h3 id="3-statistical-pos-tagging" style="text-align:left"><b><strong>3. Statistical POS Tagging </strong></b></h3><p dir="ltr"><span>It uses probabilistic models to assign grammatical categories (e.g noun, verb, adjective) to words in a text. Unlike rule-based methods which rely on handcrafted rules, it learns patterns from large annotated corpora using machine learning techniques.</span></p><p dir="ltr"><span>These models calculate the likelihood of a tag based on a word and its context, helping to resolve ambiguities and handle complex grammar. Common models include:</span></p><ul><li value="1"><a href="https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/machine-learning/hidden-markov-model-in-machine-learning/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><b><strong>Hidden Markov Models (HMMs)</strong></b></a></li><li value="2"><a href="https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/nlp/conditional-random-fields-crfs-for-pos-tagging-in-nlp/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><b><strong>Conditional Random Fields (CRFs)</strong></b></a></li></ul><h2 id="implementation-of-partsofspeech-tagging-using-nltk" style="text-align:left"><b><strong>Implementing POS Tagging with NLTK</strong></b></h2><p dir="ltr"><span>Let\'s see step by step process how POS Tagging works with NLTK:</span></p><h3 id="step-1-installing-nltk-and-downloading-necessary-resources" style="text-align:left"><b><strong>Step 1: Installing Required Resources</strong></b></h3><p dir="ltr"><span>Here we import the </span><a href="https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/python/nltk-nlp/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><span>NLTK</span></a><span> library and download the necessary datasets using nltk.download().</span></p><gfg-tabs data-mode="light" data-run-ide="true">\n            <gfg-tab slot="tab">Python</gfg-tab>\n<gfg-panel slot="panel" data-code-lang="python3" data-main-code-start="None" data-main-code-end="None">\n    <code class="language-python3"><div class=highlight><pre><span></span><span class=kn>import</span> <span class=nn>nltk</span>\n<span class=kn>from</span> <span class=nn>nltk.tokenize</span> <span class=kn>import</span> <span class=n>word_tokenize</span>\n<span class=kn>from</span> <span class=nn>nltk</span> <span class=kn>import</span> <span class=n>pos_tag</span>\n<span class=n>nltk</span><span class=o>.</span><span class=n>download</span><span class=p>(</span><span class=s1>&#39;punkt_tab&#39;</span><span class=p>)</span>\n<span class=n>nltk</span><span class=o>.</span><span class=n>download</span><span class=p>(</span><span class=s1>&#39;averaged_perceptron_tagger_eng&#39;</span><span class=p>)</span>\n</pre></div></code>\n</gfg-panel></gfg-tabs><h3 id="step-2-pos-tagging" style="text-align:left"><b><strong>Step 2: Applying POS Tagging</strong></b></h3><p dir="ltr"><span>First we store the sentence and tokenize it into words using </span><b><strong>word_tokenize(text)</strong></b><span>. Then we apply POS tagging to the tokenized words using </span><b><strong>pos_tag(words).</strong></b><span> This assigns a part-of-speech to each word.</span></p><gfg-tabs data-mode="light" data-run-ide="true">\n            <gfg-tab slot="tab">Python</gfg-tab>\n<gfg-panel slot="panel" data-code-lang="python3" data-main-code-start="None" data-main-code-end="None">\n    <code class="language-python3"><div class=highlight><pre><span></span><span class=n>text</span> <span class=o>=</span> <span class=s2>&quot;NLTK is a powerful library for natural language processing.&quot;</span>\n<span class=n>words</span> <span class=o>=</span> <span class=n>word_tokenize</span><span class=p>(</span><span class=n>text</span><span class=p>)</span>\n\n<span class=n>pos_tags</span> <span class=o>=</span> <span class=n>pos_tag</span><span class=p>(</span><span class=n>words</span><span class=p>)</span>\n</pre></div></code>\n</gfg-panel></gfg-tabs><h3 id="step-3-display-results" style="text-align:left"><span>Step 3: Displaying Results</span></h3><p dir="ltr"><span>Now we print the original sentence and loop through the tagged words to show each word with its POS tag.</span></p><gfg-tabs data-mode="light" data-run-ide="true">\n            <gfg-tab slot="tab">Python</gfg-tab>\n<gfg-panel slot="panel" data-code-lang="python3" data-main-code-start="None" data-main-code-end="None">\n    <code class="language-python3"><div class=highlight><pre><span></span><span class=nb>print</span><span class=p>(</span><span class=s2>&quot;Original Text:&quot;</span><span class=p>)</span>\n<span class=nb>print</span><span class=p>(</span><span class=n>text</span><span class=p>)</span>\n\n<span class=nb>print</span><span class=p>(</span><span class=s2>&quot;</span><span class=se>\\n</span><span class=s2>PoS Tagging Result:&quot;</span><span class=p>)</span>\n<span class=k>for</span> <span class=n>word</span><span class=p>,</span> <span class=n>pos_tag</span> <span class=ow>in</span> <span class=n>pos_tags</span><span class=p>:</span>\n    <span class=nb>print</span><span class=p>(</span><span class=sa>f</span><span class=s2>&quot;</span><span class=si>{</span><span class=n>word</span><span class=si>}</span><span class=s2>: </span><span class=si>{</span><span class=n>pos_tag</span><span id="advantages-and-disadvantages" style="text-align:left"><span>Advantages </span></h2><ol><li value="1"><b><strong>Text Simplification</strong></b><span>: POS tagging can break down complex sentences into simpler parts, making them easier to understand.</span></li><li value="2"><b><strong>Improved Search</strong></b><span>: It improves information retrieval by categorizing words, making it easier to index and search text.</span></li><li value="3"><b><strong>Named Entity Recognition (NER)</strong></b><span>: It helps identify names, places and organizations by recognizing the role of words in a sentence.</span></li></ol><h2 id="disadvantages" style="text-align:left"><span>Challenges</span></h2><ol><li value="1"><b><strong>Ambiguity</strong></b><span>: Words can have multiple meanings depending on the context which can make tagging difficult.</span></li><li value="2"><b><strong>Idiomatic Expressions</strong></b><span>: Informal language and idioms may be hard to tag correctly.</span></li><li value="3"><b><strong>Out-of-Vocabulary Words</strong></b><span>: Words that haven\xe2\x80\x99t been seen before can lead to incorrect tagging.</span></li><li value="4"><b><strong>Domain Dependence</strong></b><span>: Models may not work well outside the specific language domain they were trained on.</span></li></ol></div></div></div></div></div></div><div Tagging\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/h3\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eConsider the sentence: \\"\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eThe quick brown fox jumps over value=\\"6\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"over\\" is tagged as preposition (IN)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"7\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"the\\" is tagged as determiner (DT)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"8\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"lazy\\" is tagged as adjective (JJ)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"9\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"dog\\" is tagged as noun (NN)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003c/ul\\u003e\\u003c/blockquote\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eEach word is assigned a tag based on its role in the sentence. For example, \\"quick\\" and \\"brown\\" are adjectives that describe the noun \\"fox.\\"\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\u003ch2 id=\\"working-of-pos-tagging\\" style=\\"text-align:left\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eWorking\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/h2\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eLet\xe2\x80\x99s see various steps involved in POS tagging:\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\u003cul\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"1\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eTokenization\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e: The input text is split into individual tokens (words or subwords), this step is necessary for further analysis.\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"2\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003ePreprocessing\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e: The text is cleaned such as converting it to lowercase and removing special characters, to improve accuracy.\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"3\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eLoading a Language Model\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e: Tools like \\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003ca href=\\"https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/python/nltk-nlp/\\" rel=\\"noopener\\" target=\\"_blank\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eNLTK \\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/a\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eor \\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003ca href=\\"https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/machine-learning/python-pos-tagging-and-lemmatization-using-spacy/\\" rel=\\"noopener\\" target=\\"_blank\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eSpaCy \\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/a\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003euse pre-trained language models to understand the grammatical rules of the language, these models have been trained on large datasets.\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"4\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eLinguistic Analysis\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e: The structure of the sentence is analyzed to understand the role of each word in context.\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"5\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003ePOS Tagging\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e: Each word is assigned a part-of-speech label based on its role in the sentence and the context provided by surrounding words.\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"6\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eEvaluation\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e: The results are checked for accuracy. If there are any errors or misclassifications, they are corrected.\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003c/ul\\u003e\\u003ch2 id=\\"types-of-pos-tagging-in-nlp\\" style=\\"text-align:left\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eTypes of POS Tagging\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/h2\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eThere are different types and each has its strengths and use cases. Let\'s see few common methods:\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\u003ch3 id=\\"1-rulebased-tagging\\" style=\\"text-align:left\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e1. \\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eRule-Based Tagging\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003c/h3\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\"\\u003e\\u003ca href=\\"https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/nlp/nlp-part-of-speech-default-tagging/\\" rel=\\"noopener\\" target=\\"_blank\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eRule-based POS tagging\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/a\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e assigns POS tags based on predefined grammatical rules. These rules are crafted based on morphological features (like word endings) and syntactic context, making the approach highly interpretable and transparent.\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\" style=\\"text-align: left;\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eExample:\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003e1. Rule:\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e Assign the POS tag \\"Noun\\" to words ending in \\"-tion\\" or \\"-ment\\".\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003e2. Sentence:\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e \\"The presentation highlighted the key achievements of the project\'s development.\\"\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003e3. Tagged Output:\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\u003cul\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"1\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"presentation\\" \xe2\x86\x92 Noun (N)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"2\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"highlighted\\" \xe2\x86\x92 Verb (V)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"3\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"development\\" \xe2\x86\x92 Noun (N)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003c/ul\\u003e\\u003ch3 id=\\"2-transformationbased-tagging-tbt\\" style=\\"text-align:left\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e2. \\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eTransformation-Based Tagging (TBT)\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003c/h3\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eTBT refines POS tags through a series of context-based transformations. Unlike statistical taggers that rely on probabilities or rule-based taggers, it starts with initial tags and improves them iteratively by applying transformation rules.\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\" style=\\"text-align: left;\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eExample:\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\u003cul\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"1\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eText:\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e \\"The cat chased the mouse.\\"\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"2\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eInitial Tags:\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e \\"The\\" \xe2\x80\x93 DET, \\"cat\\" \xe2\x80\x93 NOUN, \\"chased\\" \xe2\x80\x93 VERB, \\"the\\" \xe2\x80\x93 DET, \\"mouse\\" \xe2\x80\x93 NOUN\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"3\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eRule Applied:\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e Change \xe2\x80\x9cchased\xe2\x80\x9d from Verb to Nounbecause it follows \xe2\x80\x9cthe\xe2\x80\x9d.\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"4\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eUpdated Tags:\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e \\"chased\\" becomes Noun.\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003c/ul\\u003e\\u003ch3 id=\\"3-statistical-pos-tagging\\" style=\\"text-align:left\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003e3. value=\\"1\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eParts of Speech\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e: These are categories like nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, etc that data used to train POS taggers.\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003c/ol\\u003e\\u003ch3 id=\\"example-of-pos-tagging\\" style=\\"text-align:left\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eExample of POS Tagging\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/h3\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eConsider the sentence: \\"\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eThe quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eAfter performing POS Tagging, we get:\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\u003cblockquote\\u003e\\u003cul\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"1\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"The\\" is tagged as determiner (DT)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"2\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"quick\\" is tagged as adjective (JJ)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"3\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"brown\\" is tagged as adjective (JJ)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"4\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"fox\\" is tagged as noun (NN)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"5\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"jumps\\" is tagged as verb (VBZ)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"6\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"over\\" is tagged as preposition (IN)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"7\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"the\\" is tagged as determiner (DT)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"8\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"lazy\\" is tagged as adjective (JJ)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"9\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"dog\\" is tagged as noun (NN)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003c/ul\\u003e\\u003c/blockquote\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eEach word is assigned a tag based on its role in the sentence. For example, \\"quick\\" and \\"brown\\" are adjectives that describe the noun \\"fox.\\"\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\u003ch2 id=\\"working-of-pos-tagging\\" Tagging\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/h3\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eConsider the sentence: \\"\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eThe quick brown fox jumps over get:\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\u003cblockquote\\u003e\\u003cul\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"1\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"The\\" is tagged as determiner (DT)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"2\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"quick\\" is tagged as adjective (JJ)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"3\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"brown\\" is tagged as adjective (JJ)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"4\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"fox\\" is tagged as noun (NN)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"5\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"jumps\\" is tagged as verb (VBZ)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"6\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"over\\" is tagged as preposition (IN)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"7\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"the\\" is tagged as determiner (DT)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"8\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"lazy\\" is tagged as adjective (JJ)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"9\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"dog\\" is tagged as noun (NN)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003c/ul\\u003e\\u003c/blockquote\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eEach word is assigned a tag based on its role in the sentence. For example, \\"quick\\" and \\"brown\\" are adjectives that describe the noun \\"fox.\\"\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\u003ch2 id=\\"working-of-pos-tagging\\" style=\\"text-align:left\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eWorking\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/h2\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eLet\xe2\x80\x99s see various steps involved in POS input text is split into individual tokens (words or subwords), this step is necessary for further analysis.\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"2\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003ePreprocessing\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e: The text is cleaned such as converting it to lowercase and removing special characters, to improve accuracy.\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"3\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eLoading a Language Model\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e: Tools like \\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003ca href=\\"https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/python/nltk-nlp/\\" rel=\\"noopener\\" target=\\"_blank\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eNLTK \\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/a\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eor \\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003ca href=\\"https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/machine-learning/python-pos-tagging-and-lemmatization-using-spacy/\\" rel=\\"noopener\\" target=\\"_blank\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eSpaCy \\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/a\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003euse pre-trained language models to understand the grammatical rules of the language, these models have been trained on large datasets.\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"4\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eLinguistic Analysis\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e: The structure of the sentence is analyzed to understand the role of each word in context.\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"5\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003ePOS Tagging\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e: Each word is assigned a part-of-speech label based on its role in the sentence and the context provided by surrounding words.\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"6\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eEvaluation\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e: The results are checked for accuracy. If there are any errors or misclassifications, they are corrected.\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003c/ul\\u003e\\u003ch2 id=\\"types-of-pos-tagging-in-nlp\\" style=\\"text-align:left\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eTypes of POS Tagging\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/h2\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eThere are different types and each has its strengths and use cases. Let\'s see few common methods:\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\u003ch3 id=\\"1-rulebased-tagging\\" style=\\"text-align:left\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e1. \\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eRule-Based Tagging\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003c/h3\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\"\\u003e\\u003ca href=\\"https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/nlp/nlp-part-of-speech-default-tagging/\\" rel=\\"noopener\\" target=\\"_blank\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eRule-based POS tagging\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/a\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e assigns POS tags based on predefined grammatical rules. These rules are crafted based on morphological features (like word endings) and syntactic context, making the approach highly interpretable and transparent.\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\" style=\\"text-align: left;\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eExample:\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003e1. Rule:\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e Assign the POS tag \\"Noun\\" to words ending in \\"-tion\\" or \\"-ment\\".\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003e2. Sentence:\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e \\"The presentation highlighted the key achievements of the project\'s development.\\"\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003e3. Tagged Output:\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\u003cul\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"1\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"presentation\\" \xe2\x86\x92 Noun (N)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"2\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"highlighted\\" \xe2\x86\x92 Verb (V)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"3\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e\\"development\\" \xe2\x86\x92 Noun (N)\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003c/ul\\u003e\\u003ch3 id=\\"2-transformationbased-tagging-tbt\\" style=\\"text-align:left\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e2. \\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eTransformation-Based Tagging (TBT)\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003c/h3\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eTBT refines POS tags through a series of context-based transformations. Unlike statistical taggers that rely on probabilities or rule-based taggers, it starts with initial tags and improves them iteratively by applying transformation rules.\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\" style=\\"text-align: left;\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eExample:\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\u003cul\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"1\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eText:\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e \\"The cat chased the mouse.\\"\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"2\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eInitial Tags:\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e \\"The\\" \xe2\x80\x93 DET, \\"cat\\" \xe2\x80\x93 NOUN, \\"chased\\" \xe2\x80\x93 VERB, \\"the\\" \xe2\x80\x93 DET, \\"mouse\\" \xe2\x80\x93 NOUN\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"3\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eRule Applied:\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e Change \xe2\x80\x9cchased\xe2\x80\x9d from Verb to Nounbecause it follows \xe2\x80\x9cthe\xe2\x80\x9d.\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"4\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003eUpdated Tags:\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003e \\"chased\\" becomes Noun.\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003c/ul\\u003e\\u003ch3 id=\\"3-statistical-pos-tagging\\" style=\\"text-align:left\\"\\u003e\\u003cb\\u003e\\u003cstrong\\u003e3. Statistical POS Tagging \\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003c/h3\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eIt uses probabilistic models to assign grammatical categories (e.g noun, verb, adjective) to words in a text. Unlike rule-based methods which rely on handcrafted rules, it learns patterns from large annotated corpora using machine learning techniques.\\u003c/span\\u003e\\u003c/p\\u003e\\u003cp dir=\\"ltr\\"\\u003e\\u003cspan\\u003eThese models calculate the likelihood of a tag based on a word and its context, helping to resolve ambiguities and handle complex grammar. (HMMs)\\u003c/strong\\u003e\\u003c/b\\u003e\\u003c/a\\u003e\\u003c/li\\u003e\\u003cli value=\\"2\\"\\u003e\\u003ca         background: #29D;
        position: fixed;
        z-index: 9999;
        top: 0;
        left: 0;
        width: 100%;
        height: 3px;

      #nprogress .peg {
        display: block;
        position: absolute;
        right: 0px;
        width: 100px;
        height: 100%;

        opacity: 1;
        -webkit-transform: rotate(3deg) translate(0px, -4px);
        -ms-transform: rotate(3deg) translate(0px, -4px);
        transform: rotate(3deg) translate(0px, -4px);

      #nprogress .spinner {
        display: block;
        position: fixed;
        z-index: 1031;
        top: 15px;
        right: 15px;
      }

        width: 18px;
        height: 18px;
        box-sizing: border-box;
        border: solid 2px transparent;
        border-top-color: #29D;
        border-left-color: #29D;
        border-radius: 50%;
        -webkit-animation: nprogresss-spinner 400ms linear infinite;
        animation: nprogress-spinner 400ms linear infinite;
      }
      .nprogress-custom-parent {
        overflow: hidden;
        position: relative;
      }
      .nprogress-custom-parent #nprogress .spinner,
      .nprogress-custom-parent #nprogress .bar {
        position: absolute;
      }
      @-webkit-keyframes nprogress-spinner {
        0% {
          -webkit-transform: rotate(0deg);
        }
        100% {
          -webkit-transform: rotate(360deg);
        }
      }

          transform: rotate(0deg);
        }

class="ArticleHeader_last_updated_parent--date__O011V"><span>Last Updated : </span><span>2 Jul, 2026</span></div><div class="ArticleHeader_last_updated_parent--three_dot_dropdown__yslcL"><div styles="[object Object]"><div class="ArticleThreeDot_threedotcontainer__dfGWD"><div class="ArticleThreeDot_comment__gJfFl" style="background-position:0px 0px"></div><div class="ArticleThreeDot_improve___NFbl" style="background-position:-40px -521px"></div><div class="ArticleThreeDot_threedot-wrapper__q4ELY"><ul class="ArticleThreeDot_threedot__ZQ19q"><li></li><li></li><li></li></ul></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="MainArticleContent_articleMainContentCss__b_1_R article--viewer_content"><div class="a-wrapper"><div class="content"><div class="text"><div class="html-chunk"><p dir="ltr"><span>Parts of Speech (PoS) tagging is a fundamental task in Natural Language Processing (NLP) where each word in a sentence is assigned a grammatical category such as noun, verb, adjective or adverb. </span></p><ul><li value="1"><span>This process help machines to understand the structure and meaning of sentences by identifying the roles of words and their relationships.</span></li><li value="2"><span>Analyzes the context of words to determine their correct part of speech</span></li><li value="3"><span>Improves text analysis, parsing, machine translation, and information extraction</span></li><li value="4"><span>Widely used in text classification, sentiment analysis, chatbots, and search engine</span></li></ul><gfg-carousel><gfg-carousel-content alt="a_quick_brown_fox_jumps_over_a_lazy_dog.webp" height="400" src="https://media.geeksforgeeks.org/wp-content/uploads/20250819114114256836/a_quick_brown_fox_jumps_over_a_lazy_dog.webp" width="800"></gfg-carousel-content><gfg-carousel-content alt="architecture_of_pos_tagging.webp" height="400" src="https://media.geeksforgeeks.org/wp-content/uploads/20250819114113512745/architecture_of_pos_tagging.webp" width="800"></gfg-carousel-content><gfg-carousel-content alt="types_of_pos_tagging_.webp" height="400" src="https://media.geeksforgeeks.org/wp-content/uploads/20250819114112908101/types_of_pos_tagging_.webp" width="800"></gfg-carousel-content><gfg-carousel-content alt="applications_of_pos_tagging.webp" height="400" src="https://media.geeksforgeeks.org/wp-content/uploads/20250819114113932684/applications_of_pos_tagging.webp" width="800"></gfg-carousel-content><gfg-carousel-content alt="challenges_of_pos_tagging.webp" height="400" src="https://media.geeksforgeeks.org/wp-content/uploads/20250819114113277817/challenges_of_pos_tagging.webp" width="800"></gfg-carousel-content></gfg-carousel><p dir="ltr"><span>It plays an important role in various NLP applications including machine translation, sentiment analysis and information retrieval, by bridging the gap between human language and machine understanding.</span></p><h2 id="key-concepts-in-pos-tagging" style="text-align:left"><span>Key Concepts</span></h2><ol><li value="1"><b><strong>Parts of Speech</strong></b><span>: These are categories like nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, etc that define the role of a word in a sentence.</span></li><li value="2"><b><strong>Tagging</strong></b><span>: The process of assigning a specific part-of-speech label to each word in a sentence.</span></li><li value="3"><b><strong>Corpus</strong></b><span>: A large collection of text data used to train POS taggers.</span></li></ol><h3 id="example-of-pos-tagging" style="text-align:left"><span>Example of POS Tagging</span></h3><p dir="ltr"><span>Consider the sentence: "</span><b><strong>The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.</strong></b><span>"</span></p><p dir="ltr"><span>After performing POS Tagging, we get:</span></p><blockquote><ul><li value="1"><span>"The" is tagged as determiner (DT)</span></li><li value="2"><span>"quick" is tagged as adjective (JJ)</span></li><li value="3"><span>"brown" is tagged as adjective (JJ)</span></li><li value="4"><span>"fox" is tagged as noun (NN)</span></li><li value="5"><span>"jumps" is tagged as verb (VBZ)</span></li><li value="6"><span>"over" is tagged as preposition (IN)</span></li><li value="7"><span>"the" is tagged as determiner (DT)</span></li><li value="8"><span>"lazy" is tagged as adjective (JJ)</span></li><li value="9"><span>"dog" is tagged as noun (NN)</span></li></ul></blockquote><p dir="ltr"><span>Each word is assigned a tag based on its role in the sentence. For example, "quick" and "brown" are adjectives that describe the noun "fox."</span></p><h2 id="working-of-pos-tagging" style="text-align:left"><span>Working</span></h2><p dir="ltr"><span>Let’s see various steps involved in POS tagging:</span></p><ul><li value="1"><b><strong>Tokenization</strong></b><span>: The input text is split into individual tokens (words or subwords), this step is necessary for further analysis.</span></li><li value="2"><b><strong>Preprocessing</strong></b><span>: The text is cleaned such as converting it to lowercase and removing special characters, to improve accuracy.</span></li><li value="3"><b><strong>Loading a Language Model</strong></b><span>: Tools like </span><a href="https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/python/nltk-nlp/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><span>NLTK </span></a><span>or </span><a href="https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/machine-learning/python-pos-tagging-and-lemmatization-using-spacy/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><span>SpaCy </span></a><span>use pre-trained language models to understand the grammatical rules of the language, these models have been trained on large datasets.</span></li><li value="4"><b><strong>Linguistic Analysis</strong></b><span>: The structure of the sentence is analyzed to understand the role of each word in context.</span></li><li value="5"><b><strong>POS Tagging</strong></b><span>: Each word is assigned a part-of-speech label based on its role in the sentence and the context provided by surrounding words.</span></li><li value="6"><b><strong>Evaluation</strong></b><span>: The results are checked for accuracy. If there are any errors or misclassifications, they are corrected.</span></li></ul><h2 id="types-of-pos-tagging-in-nlp" style="text-align:left"><span>Types of POS Tagging</span></h2><p dir="ltr"><span>There are different types and each has its strengths and use cases. Let's see few common methods:</span></p><h3 id="1-rulebased-tagging" style="text-align:left"><span>1. </span><b><strong>Rule-Based Tagging</strong></b></h3><p dir="ltr"><a href="https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/nlp/nlp-part-of-speech-default-tagging/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><span>Rule-based POS tagging</span></a><span> assigns POS tags based on predefined grammatical rules. These rules are crafted based on morphological features (like word endings) and syntactic context, making the approach highly interpretable and transparent.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;"><b><strong>Example:</strong></b></p><p dir="ltr"><b><strong>1. Rule:</strong></b><span> Assign the POS tag "Noun" to words ending in "-tion" or "-ment".</span></p><p dir="ltr"><b><strong>2. Sentence:</strong></b><span> "The presentation highlighted the key achievements of the project's development."</span></p><p dir="ltr"><b><strong>3. Tagged Output:</strong></b></p><ul><li value="1"><span>"presentation" → Noun (N)</span></li><li value="2"><span>"highlighted" → Verb (V)</span></li><li value="3"><span>"development" → Noun (N)</span></li></ul><h3 id="2-transformationbased-tagging-tbt" style="text-align:left"><span>2. </span><b><strong>Transformation-Based Tagging (TBT)</strong></b></h3><p dir="ltr"><span>TBT refines POS tags through a series of context-based transformations. Unlike statistical taggers that rely on probabilities or rule-based taggers, it starts with initial tags and improves them iteratively by applying transformation rules.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;"><b><strong>Example:</strong></b></p><ul><li value="1"><b><strong>Text:</strong></b><span> "The cat chased the mouse."</span></li><li value="2"><b><strong>Initial Tags:</strong></b><span> "The" – DET, "cat" – NOUN, "chased" – VERB, "the" – DET, "mouse" – NOUN</span></li><li value="3"><b><strong>Rule Applied:</strong></b><span> Change “chased” from Verb to Nounbecause it follows “the”.</span></li><li value="4"><b><strong>Updated Tags:</strong></b><span> "chased" becomes Noun.</span></li></ul><h3 id="3-statistical-pos-tagging" style="text-align:left"><b><strong>3. Statistical POS Tagging </strong></b></h3><p dir="ltr"><span>It uses probabilistic models to assign grammatical categories (e.g noun, verb, adjective) to words in a text. Unlike rule-based methods which rely on handcrafted rules, it learns patterns from large annotated corpora using machine learning techniques.</span></p><p dir="ltr"><span>These models calculate the likelihood of a tag based on a word and its context, helping to resolve ambiguities and handle complex grammar. Common models include:</span></p><ul><li value="1"><a href="https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/machine-learning/hidden-markov-model-in-machine-learning/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><b><strong>Hidden Markov Models (HMMs)</strong></b></a></li><li value="2"><a href="https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/nlp/conditional-random-fields-crfs-for-pos-tagging-in-nlp/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><b><strong>Conditional Random Fields (CRFs)</strong></b></a></li></ul><h2 id="implementation-of-partsofspeech-tagging-using-nltk" style="text-align:left"><b><strong>Implementing POS Tagging with NLTK</strong></b></h2><p dir="ltr"><span>Let's see step by step process how POS Tagging works with NLTK:</span></p><h3 id="step-1-installing-nltk-and-downloading-necessary-resources" style="text-align:left"><b><strong>Step 1: Installing Required Resources</strong></b></h3><p dir="ltr"><span>Here we import the </span><a href="https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/python/nltk-nlp/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><span>NLTK</span></a><span> library and download the necessary datasets using nltk.download().</span></p><gfg-tabs data-mode="light" data-run-ide="true">
<gfg-tab slot="tab">Python</gfg-tab>
<gfg-panel data-code-lang="python3" data-main-code-end="None" data-main-code-start="None" slot="panel">
<code class="language-python3"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="kn">import</span> <span class="nn">nltk</span>
<span class="kn">from</span> <span class="nn">nltk.tokenize</span> <span class="kn">import</span> <span class="n">word_tokenize</span>
<span class="kn">from</span> <span class="nn">nltk</span> <span class="kn">import</span> <span class="n">pos_tag</span>
<span class="n">nltk</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">download</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s1">'punkt_tab'</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="n">nltk</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">download</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s1">'averaged_perceptron_tagger_eng'</span><span class="p">)</span>
</pre></div></code>
</gfg-panel></gfg-tabs><h3 id="step-2-pos-tagging" style="text-align:left"><b><strong>Step 2: Applying POS Tagging</strong></b></h3><p dir="ltr"><span>First we store the sentence and tokenize it into words using </span><b><strong>word_tokenize(text)</strong></b><span>. Then we apply POS tagging to the tokenized words using </span><b><strong>pos_tag(words).</strong></b><span> This assigns a part-of-speech to each word.</span></p><gfg-tabs data-mode="light" data-run-ide="true">
<gfg-tab slot="tab">Python</gfg-tab>
<gfg-panel data-code-lang="python3" data-main-code-end="None" data-main-code-start="None" slot="panel">
<code class="language-python3"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="n">text</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s2">"NLTK is a powerful library for natural language processing."</span>
<span class="n">words</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">word_tokenize</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">text</span><span class="p">)</span>

<span class="n">pos_tags</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">pos_tag</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">words</span><span class="p">)</span>
</pre></div></code>
</gfg-panel></gfg-tabs><h3 id="step-3-display-results" style="text-align:left"><span>Step 3: Displaying Results</span></h3><p dir="ltr"><span>Now we print the original sentence and loop through the tagged words to show each word with its POS tag.</span></p><gfg-tabs data-mode="light" data-run-ide="true">
<gfg-tab slot="tab">Python</gfg-tab>
<gfg-panel data-code-lang="python3" data-main-code-end="None" data-main-code-start="None" slot="panel">
<code class="language-python3"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="nb">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">"Original Text:"</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="nb">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">text</span><span class="p">)</span>

<span class="nb">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s2">PoS Tagging Result:"</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">word</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">pos_tag</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="n">pos_tags</span><span class="p">:</span>
    <span class="nb">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sa">f</span><span class="s2">"</span><span class="si">{</span><span class="n">word</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2">: </span><span class="si">{</span><span class="n">pos_tag</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2">"</span><span class="p">)</span>
</pre></div></code>
</gfg-panel></gfg-tabs><p dir="ltr"><b><strong>Output:</strong></b></p><figure class="image"><img alt="pos1" height="248" src="https://media.geeksforgeeks.org/wp-content/uploads/20250812190422006361/pos1.webp" srcset="https://media.geeksforgeeks.org/wp-content/uploads/20250812190422006361/pos1.webp 462w,https://media.geeksforgeeks.org/wp-content/uploads/20250812190422006361/pos1-100.webp 100w,https://media.geeksforgeeks.org/wp-content/uploads/20250812190422006361/pos1-200.webp 200w,https://media.geeksforgeeks.org/wp-content/uploads/20250812190422006361/pos1-300.webp 300w" width="462"/><figcaption>POS Tagging with NLTK</figcaption></figure><h2 id="implementation-of-partsofspeech-tagging-using-spacy" style="text-align:left"><b><strong>Implementing POS Tagging with SpaCy</strong></b></h2><p dir="ltr" style="text-align: left;"><span>Let's see step by step process how POS Tagging works with SpaCy:</span></p><h3 id="step-1-installing-required-resources" style="text-align:left"><b><strong>Step 1: Installing and importing Required Resources</strong></b></h3><p dir="ltr"><span>Here we install and import the </span><a href="https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/machine-learning/python-pos-tagging-and-lemmatization-using-spacy/" rel="noopener" target="_blank"><span>SpaCy</span></a><span> library and install the pre-trained English language model (en_core_web_sm).</span></p><gfg-tabs data-mode="light" data-run-ide="true">
<gfg-tab slot="tab">Python</gfg-tab>
<gfg-panel data-code-lang="python3" data-main-code-end="None" data-main-code-start="None" slot="panel">
<code class="language-python3"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="err">!</span><span class="n">pip</span> <span class="n">install</span> <span class="n">spacy</span>
<span class="err">!</span><span class="n">python</span> <span class="o">-</span><span class="n">m</span> <span class="n">spacy</span> <span class="n">download</span> <span class="n">en_core_web_sm</span>
<span class="kn">import</span> <span class="nn">spacy</span>
<span class="n">nlp</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">spacy</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">load</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">"en_core_web_sm"</span><span class="p">)</span>
</pre></div></code>
</gfg-panel></gfg-tabs><h3 id="step-2-define-and-process-the-text" style="text-align:left"><b><strong>Step 2: Defining and Processing the Text</strong></b></h3><p dir="ltr"><span>We store the sentence in a variable and process it with</span><b><strong> nlp(text) </strong></b><span>to get linguistic annotations.</span></p><gfg-tabs data-mode="light" data-run-ide="true">
<gfg-tab slot="tab">Python</gfg-tab>
<gfg-panel data-code-lang="python3" data-main-code-end="None" data-main-code-start="None" slot="panel">
<code class="language-python3"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="n">text</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="s2">"SpaCy is a popular natural language processing library."</span>
<span class="n">doc</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="n">nlp</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">text</span><span class="p">)</span>
</pre></div></code>
</gfg-panel></gfg-tabs><h3 id="step-3-pos-tagging" style="text-align:left"><span>Step 3: Displaying POS Tagging</span></h3><p dir="ltr"><span>Print the original sentence then loop through the tokens and display each word with its POS tag.</span></p><gfg-tabs data-mode="light" data-run-ide="true">
<gfg-tab slot="tab">Python</gfg-tab>
<gfg-panel data-code-lang="python3" data-main-code-end="None" data-main-code-start="None" slot="panel">
<code class="language-python3"><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><span class="nb">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">"Original Text: "</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">text</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="nb">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s2">"PoS Tagging Result:"</span><span class="p">)</span>
<span class="k">for</span> <span class="n">token</span> <span class="ow">in</span> <span class="n">doc</span><span class="p">:</span>
    <span class="nb">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sa">f</span><span class="s2">"</span><span class="si">{</span><span class="n">token</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">text</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2">: </span><span class="si">{</span><span class="n">token</span><span class="o">.</span><span class="n">pos_</span><span class="si">}</span><span class="s2">"</span><span class="p">)</span>
</pre></div></code>
</gfg-panel></gfg-tabs><p dir="ltr"><b><strong>Output:</strong></b></p><figure class="image"><img alt="pos2" height="198" loading="lazy" src="https://media.geeksforgeeks.org/wp-content/uploads/20250812190447698174/pos2.webp" srcset="https://media.geeksforgeeks.org/wp-content/uploads/20250812190447698174/pos2.webp 558w,https://media.geeksforgeeks.org/wp-content/uploads/20250812190447698174/pos2-100.webp 100w,https://media.geeksforgeeks.org/wp-content/uploads/20250812190447698174/pos2-200.webp 200w,https://media.geeksforgeeks.org/wp-content/uploads/20250812190447698174/pos2-300.webp 300w" width="558"/><figcaption>POS Tagging with SpaCy</figcaption></figure><h2 id="advantages-and-disadvantages" style="text-align:left"><span>Advantages </span></h2><ol><li value="1"><b><strong>Text Simplification</strong></b><span>: POS tagging can break down complex sentences into simpler parts, making them easier to understand.</span></li><li value="2"><b><strong>Improved Search</strong></b><span>: It improves information retrieval by categorizing words, making it easier to index and search text.</span></li><li value="3"><b><strong>Named Entity Recognition (NER)</strong></b><span>: It helps identify names, places and organizations by recognizing the role of words in a sentence.</span></li></ol><h2 id="disadvantages" style="text-align:left"><span>Challenges</span></h2><ol><li value="1"><b><strong>Ambiguity</strong></b><span>: Words can have multiple meanings depending on the context which can make tagging difficult.</span></li><li value="2"><b><strong>Idiomatic Expressions</strong></b><span>: Informal language and idioms may be hard to tag correctly.</span></li><li value="3"><b><strong>Out-of-Vocabulary Words</strong></b><span>: Words that haven’t been seen before can lead to incorrect tagging.</span></li><li value="4"><b><strong>Domain Dependence</strong></b><span>: Models may not work well outside the specific language domain they were trained on.</span></li></ol></div></div></div></div></div></div><div id="__NEXT_DATA__" type="application/json">{"props":{"pageProps":{"postDataFromWriteApi":{"id":864584,"post_content":"\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eParts of Speech (PoS) tagging is a \u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\u003cli value=\"1\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eThis process help machines to understand the structure and meaning of sentences by identifying the roles of words and their relationships.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"2\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAnalyzes the context of words to determine their correct part of speech\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"3\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eImproves text analysis, parsing, machine translation, and information extraction\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"4\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eWidely used in text classification, sentiment analysis, chatbots, and search translation, sentiment analysis and information retrieval, by bridging the gap between human language and machine understanding.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch2 id=\"key-concepts-in-pos-tagging\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eKey Concepts\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e\u003col\u003e\u003cli value=\"1\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eParts of Speech\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: These are categories like nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, etc that define the role of a word in a sentence.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"2\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTagging\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: The process of assigning a specific part-of-speech label to each word in a sentence.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"3\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCorpus\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: A large collection of text data used to train POS taggers.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"example-of-pos-tagging\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eExample of POS Tagging\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eConsider the sentence: \"\u003c/span\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eThe quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAfter performing POS Tagging, we get:\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cblockquote\u003e\u003cul\u003e\u003cli value=\"1\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"The\" is tagged as determiner (DT)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"2\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"quick\" is tagged as adjective (JJ)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"3\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"brown\" is tagged as adjective (JJ)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"4\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"fox\" is tagged as noun (NN)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"5\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"jumps\" is tagged as verb (VBZ)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"6\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"over\" is tagged as preposition (IN)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"7\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"the\" is tagged as determiner (DT)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"8\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"lazy\" is tagged as adjective (JJ)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"9\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"dog\" is tagged as noun (NN)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\u003c/blockquote\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eEach word is assigned a tag based on its role in the sentence. For example, \"quick\" and \"brown\" are adjectives that describe the noun \"fox.\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch2 id=\"working-of-pos-tagging\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eWorking\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eLet’s see various steps involved in POS tagging:\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\u003cli value=\"1\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTokenization\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: The input text is split into individual tokens (words or subwords), this step is necessary for further analysis.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"2\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePreprocessing\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: The text is cleaned such as converting it to lowercase and removing special characters, to improve accuracy.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"3\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLoading a Language Model\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: Tools like \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/python/nltk-nlp/\" rel=\"noopener\" target=\"_blank\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eNLTK \u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003eor \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/machine-learning/python-pos-tagging-and-lemmatization-using-spacy/\" rel=\"noopener\" target=\"_blank\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eSpaCy \u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003euse pre-trained language models to understand the grammatical rules of the language, these models have been trained on large datasets.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"4\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLinguistic Analysis\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: The structure of the sentence is analyzed to understand the role of each word in context.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"5\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePOS Tagging\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: Each word is assigned a part-of-speech label based on its role in the sentence and the context provided by surrounding words.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"6\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eEvaluation\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: The results are checked for accuracy. If there are any errors or misclassifications, they are corrected.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\u003ch2 id=\"types-of-pos-tagging-in-nlp\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eTypes of POS Tagging\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eThere are different types and each has its strengths and use cases. Let's see few common methods:\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"1-rulebased-tagging\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e1. \u003c/span\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRule-Based Tagging\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/nlp/nlp-part-of-speech-default-tagging/\" rel=\"noopener\" target=\"_blank\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eRule-based POS tagging\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e assigns POS tags based on predefined grammatical rules. These rules are crafted based on morphological features (like word endings) and syntactic context, making the approach highly interpretable and transparent.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExample:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e1. Rule:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e Assign the POS tag \"Noun\" to words ending in \"-tion\" or \"-ment\".\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e2. Sentence:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e \"The presentation highlighted the key achievements of the project's development.\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e3. Tagged Output:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\u003cli value=\"1\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"presentation\" → Noun (N)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"2\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"highlighted\" → Verb (V)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"3\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"development\" → Noun (N)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"2-transformationbased-tagging-tbt\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e2. \u003c/span\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTransformation-Based Tagging (TBT)\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eTBT refines POS tags through a series of context-based transformations. Unlike statistical taggers that rely on probabilities or rule-based taggers, it starts with initial tags and improves them iteratively by applying transformation rules.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExample:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\u003cli value=\"1\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eText:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e \"The cat chased the mouse.\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"2\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eInitial Tags:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e \"The\" – DET, \"cat\" – NOUN, \"chased\" – VERB, \"the\" – DET, \"mouse\" – NOUN\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"3\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRule Applied:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e Change “chased” from Verb to Nounbecause it follows “the”.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"4\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUpdated Tags:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e \"chased\" becomes Noun.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"3-statistical-pos-tagging\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e3. Statistical POS Tagging \u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eIt uses probabilistic models to assign grammatical categories (e.g noun, verb, adjective) to words in a text. Unlike rule-based methods which rely on handcrafted rules, it learns patterns from large annotated corpora using machine learning techniques.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eThese models calculate the likelihood of a tag based on a word and its context, helping to resolve ambiguities and handle complex grammar. Common models include:\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\u003cli value=\"1\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/machine-learning/hidden-markov-model-in-machine-learning/\" rel=\"noopener\" target=\"_blank\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eHidden Markov Models (HMMs)\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"2\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/nlp/conditional-random-fields-crfs-for-pos-tagging-in-nlp/\" rel=\"noopener\" target=\"_blank\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eConditional Random Fields (CRFs)\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\u003ch2 id=\"implementation-of-partsofspeech-tagging-using-nltk\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eImplementing POS Tagging with NLTK\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eLet's see step by step process how POS Tagging works with NLTK:\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"step-1-installing-nltk-and-downloading-necessary-resources\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eStep 1: Installing Required Resources\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eHere we import the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/python/nltk-nlp/\" rel=\"noopener\" target=\"_blank\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eNLTK\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e library and download the necessary datasets using nltk.download().\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e[GFGTABS]\u003cgfg-tabs data-mode=\"light\" data-run-ide=\"true\"\u003e\n            \u003cgfg-tab slot=\"tab\"\u003ePython\u003c/gfg-tab\u003e\n\u003cgfg-panel slot=\"panel\" data-code-lang=\"python3\" data-main-code-start=\"None\" data-main-code-end=\"None\"\u003e\n    \u003ccode \u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\u003cli value=\"1\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eThis process help machines to understand the structure and meaning of sentences by identifying the roles of words
