width=\"800\"\u003e\u003c/gfg-carousel-content\u003e\u003c/gfg-carousel\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eIt plays an important role in various NLP applications including machine translation, sentiment analysis and information retrieval, by bridging the gap between human language and machine understanding.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch2 id=\"key-concepts-in-pos-tagging\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eKey Concepts\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e\u003col\u003e\u003cli value=\"1\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eParts of Speech\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: These are categories like nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, etc that define the role of a word in a sentence.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"2\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTagging\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: The process of assigning a specific part-of-speech label to each word in a sentence.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"3\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCorpus\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: A large collection of text data used to train POS taggers.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"example-of-pos-tagging\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eExample of POS Tagging\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eConsider the sentence: \"\u003c/span\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eThe quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAfter performing POS Tagging, we get:\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cblockquote\u003e\u003cul\u003e\u003cli value=\"1\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"The\" is tagged as determiner (DT)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"2\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"quick\" is tagged as adjective (JJ)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"3\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"brown\" is tagged as adjective (JJ)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"4\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"fox\" is tagged as noun (NN)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"5\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"jumps\" is tagged as verb (VBZ)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"6\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"over\" is tagged as preposition (IN)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"7\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"the\" is tagged as determiner (DT)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"8\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"lazy\" is tagged as adjective (JJ)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"9\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"dog\" is tagged as noun (NN)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\u003c/blockquote\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eEach word is assigned a tag based on its role in the sentence. For example, \"quick\" and \"brown\" are adjectives that describe the noun \"fox.\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch2 id=\"working-of-pos-tagging\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eWorking\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eLet’s see various steps involved in POS tagging:\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\u003cli value=\"1\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTokenization\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: The input text is split into individual tokens (words or subwords), this step is necessary for further analysis.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"2\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePreprocessing\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: The text is cleaned such as converting it to lowercase and removing special characters, to improve accuracy.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"3\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLoading a Language Model\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: Tools like \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/python/nltk-nlp/\" rel=\"noopener\" target=\"_blank\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eNLTK \u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003eor \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/machine-learning/python-pos-tagging-and-lemmatization-using-spacy/\" rel=\"noopener\" target=\"_blank\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eSpaCy \u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003euse pre-trained language models to understand the grammatical rules of the language, these models have been trained on large datasets.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"4\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLinguistic Analysis\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: The structure of the sentence is analyzed to understand the role of each word in context.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"5\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePOS Tagging\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: Each word is assigned a part-of-speech label based on its role in the sentence and the context provided by surrounding words.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"6\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eEvaluation\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: The results are checked for accuracy. If there are any errors or misclassifications, they are corrected.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\u003ch2 id=\"types-of-pos-tagging-in-nlp\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eTypes of POS Tagging\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eThere are different types and each has its strengths and use cases. Let's see few common methods:\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"1-rulebased-tagging\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e1. \u003c/span\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRule-Based Tagging\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/nlp/nlp-part-of-speech-default-tagging/\" rel=\"noopener\" target=\"_blank\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eRule-based POS tagging\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e assigns POS tags based on predefined grammatical rules. These rules are crafted based on morphological features (like word endings) and syntactic context, making the approach highly interpretable and transparent.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExample:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e1. Rule:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e Assign the POS tag \"Noun\" to words ending in \"-tion\" or \"-ment\".\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e2. Sentence:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e \"The presentation highlighted the key achievements of the project's development.\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e3. Tagged Output:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\u003cli value=\"1\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"presentation\" → Noun (N)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"2\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"highlighted\" → Verb (V)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"3\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"development\" → Noun (N)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"2-transformationbased-tagging-tbt\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e2. \u003c/span\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTransformation-Based Tagging (TBT)\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eTBT refines POS tags through a series of context-based transformations. Unlike statistical taggers that rely on probabilities or rule-based taggers, it starts with initial tags and improves them iteratively by applying transformation rules.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExample:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\u003cli value=\"1\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eText:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e \"The cat chased the mouse.\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"2\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eInitial Tags:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e \"The\" – DET, \"cat\" – NOUN, \"chased\" – VERB, \"the\" – DET, \"mouse\" – NOUN\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"3\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRule Applied:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e Change “chased” from Verb to Nounbecause it follows “the”.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"4\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUpdated Tags:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e \"chased\" becomes Noun.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"3-statistical-pos-tagging\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e3. Statistical POS Tagging \u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eIt uses probabilistic models to assign grammatical categories (e.g noun, verb, adjective) to words in a text. Unlike rule-based methods which rely on handcrafted rules, it learns patterns from large annotated corpora using machine learning techniques.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eThese models calculate the likelihood of a tag based on a word and its context, helping to resolve ambiguities and handle complex grammar. Common models include:\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\u003cli value=\"1\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/machine-learning/hidden-markov-model-in-machine-learning/\" rel=\"noopener\" target=\"_blank\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eHidden Markov Models (HMMs)\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"2\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/nlp/conditional-random-fields-crfs-for-pos-tagging-in-nlp/\" rel=\"noopener\" target=\"_blank\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eConditional Random Fields (CRFs)\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\u003ch2 id=\"implementation-of-partsofspeech-tagging-using-nltk\" \u003c/span\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e\u003col\u003e\u003cli value=\"1\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eText Simplification\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: POS tagging can break down complex sentences into simpler parts, making them easier to understand.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"2\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eImproved Search\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: It improves information retrieval by categorizing words, making it easier to index and search text.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"3\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eNamed Entity Recognition (NER)\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: It helps identify names, places and organizations by recognizing the role of words in a sentence.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\u003ch2 id=\"disadvantages\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eChallenges\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e\u003col\u003e\u003cli value=\"1\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAmbiguity\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: Words can have multiple meanings depending on the context which can make tagging difficult.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"2\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eIdiomatic Expressions\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: Informal language and idioms may be hard to tag correctly.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"3\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOut-of-Vocabulary Words\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: Words that haven’t been seen before can lead to incorrect tagging.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"4\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDomain Dependence\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: Models may not work well outside the specific language domain they were trained width=\"800\"\u003e\u003c/gfg-carousel-content\u003e\u003c/gfg-carousel\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eIt plays an important role in various NLP applications including machine translation, sentiment analysis and information retrieval, by bridging the gap between human language and machine understanding.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch2 id=\"key-concepts-in-pos-tagging\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eKey Concepts\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e\u003col\u003e\u003cli value=\"1\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eParts of Speech\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: These are categories like nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, etc that define the role of a word in a sentence.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"2\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTagging\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: The process of assigning a specific part-of-speech label to each word in a sentence.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"3\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCorpus\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: A large collection of text data used to train POS taggers.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ol\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"example-of-pos-tagging\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eExample of POS Tagging\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eConsider the sentence: \"\u003c/span\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eThe quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eAfter performing POS Tagging, we get:\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cblockquote\u003e\u003cul\u003e\u003cli value=\"1\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"The\" is tagged as determiner (DT)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"2\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"quick\" is tagged as adjective (JJ)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"3\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"brown\" is tagged as adjective (JJ)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"4\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"fox\" is tagged as noun (NN)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"5\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"jumps\" is tagged as verb (VBZ)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"6\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"over\" is tagged as preposition (IN)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"7\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"the\" is tagged as determiner (DT)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"8\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"lazy\" is tagged as adjective (JJ)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"9\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"dog\" is tagged as noun (NN)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\u003c/blockquote\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eEach word is assigned a tag based on its role in the sentence. For example, \"quick\" and \"brown\" are adjectives that describe the noun \"fox.\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch2 id=\"working-of-pos-tagging\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eWorking\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eLet’s see various steps involved in POS tagging:\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\u003cli value=\"1\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTokenization\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: The input text is split into individual tokens (words or subwords), this step is necessary for further analysis.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"2\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePreprocessing\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: The text is cleaned such as converting it to lowercase and removing special characters, to improve accuracy.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"3\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLoading a Language Model\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: Tools like \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/python/nltk-nlp/\" rel=\"noopener\" target=\"_blank\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eNLTK \u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003eor \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/machine-learning/python-pos-tagging-and-lemmatization-using-spacy/\" rel=\"noopener\" target=\"_blank\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eSpaCy \u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003euse pre-trained language models to understand the grammatical rules of the language, these models have been trained on large datasets.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"4\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLinguistic Analysis\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: The structure of the sentence is analyzed to understand the role of each word in context.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"5\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003ePOS Tagging\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: Each word is assigned a part-of-speech label based on its role in the sentence and the context provided by surrounding words.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"6\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eEvaluation\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e: The results are checked for accuracy. If there are any errors or misclassifications, they are corrected.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\u003ch2 id=\"types-of-pos-tagging-in-nlp\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eTypes of POS Tagging\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eThere are different types and each has its strengths and use cases. Let's see few common methods:\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"1-rulebased-tagging\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e1. \u003c/span\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRule-Based Tagging\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/nlp/nlp-part-of-speech-default-tagging/\" rel=\"noopener\" target=\"_blank\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eRule-based POS tagging\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e assigns POS tags based on predefined grammatical rules. These rules are crafted based on morphological features (like word endings) and syntactic context, making the approach highly interpretable and transparent.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExample:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e1. Rule:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e Assign the POS tag \"Noun\" to words ending in \"-tion\" or \"-ment\".\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e2. Sentence:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e \"The presentation highlighted the key achievements of the project's development.\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e3. Tagged Output:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\u003cli value=\"1\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"presentation\" → Noun (N)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"2\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"highlighted\" → Verb (V)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"3\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e\"development\" → Noun (N)\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"2-transformationbased-tagging-tbt\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003e2. \u003c/span\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTransformation-Based Tagging (TBT)\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eTBT refines POS tags through a series of context-based transformations. Unlike statistical taggers that rely on probabilities or rule-based taggers, it starts with initial tags and improves them iteratively by applying transformation rules.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\" style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExample:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\u003cli value=\"1\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eText:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e \"The cat chased the mouse.\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"2\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eInitial Tags:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e \"The\" – DET, \"cat\" – NOUN, \"chased\" – VERB, \"the\" – DET, \"mouse\" – NOUN\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"3\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRule Applied:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e Change “chased” from Verb to Nounbecause it follows “the”.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"4\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUpdated Tags:\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e \"chased\" becomes Noun.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"3-statistical-pos-tagging\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e3. Statistical POS Tagging \u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eIt uses probabilistic models to assign grammatical categories (e.g noun, verb, adjective) to words in a text. Unlike rule-based methods which rely on handcrafted rules, it learns patterns from large annotated corpora using machine learning techniques.\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eThese models calculate the likelihood of a tag based on a word and its context, helping to resolve ambiguities and handle complex grammar. Common models include:\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\u003cli value=\"1\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/machine-learning/hidden-markov-model-in-machine-learning/\" rel=\"noopener\" target=\"_blank\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eHidden Markov Models (HMMs)\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003cli value=\"2\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/nlp/conditional-random-fields-crfs-for-pos-tagging-in-nlp/\" rel=\"noopener\" target=\"_blank\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eConditional Random Fields (CRFs)\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\u003c/ul\u003e\u003ch2 id=\"implementation-of-partsofspeech-tagging-using-nltk\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eImplementing POS Tagging with NLTK\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/h2\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eLet's see step by step process how POS Tagging works with NLTK:\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"step-1-installing-nltk-and-downloading-necessary-resources\" style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eStep 1: Installing Required Resources\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eHere we import the \u003c/span\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/python/nltk-nlp/\" rel=\"noopener\" target=\"_blank\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eNLTK\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003cspan\u003e style=\"text-align:left\"\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eStep 2: Applying POS Tagging\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp dir=\"ltr\"\u003e\u003cspan\u003eFirst we store the sentence and tokenize it into words using \u003c/span\u003e\u003cb\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eword_tokenize(text)\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/b\u003e\u003cspan\u003e. 360 courseexplorepos(parts-of-speech) tagging in nlplast updated : 2 jul, 2026parts of speech (pos) tagging is a fundamental task in natural language processing (nlp) where each word in a sentence is assigned a grammatical category such as noun, verb, adjective or adverb. this process help machines to understand the structure and meaning of sentences by identifying the roles of words and their relationships.analyzes the context of words to determine their correct part of speechimproves text analysis, parsing, machine translation, and information extractionwidely used in text classification, sentiment analysis, chatbots, and search engineit plays an important role in various nlp applications including machine translation, sentiment analysis and information retrieval, by bridging the gap between human language and machine understanding.key conceptsparts of speech: these are categories like nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, etc that define the role of a word in a sentence.tagging: the process of assigning a specific part-of-speech label to each word in a sentence.corpus: a large collection of text data used to train pos taggers.example of pos taggingconsider the sentence: "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog."after performing pos tagging, we get:"the" is tagged as determiner (dt)"quick" is tagged as adjective (jj)"brown" is tagged as adjective (jj)"fox" is tagged as noun (nn)"jumps" is tagged as verb (vbz)"over" is tagged as preposition (in)"the" is tagged as determiner (dt)"lazy" is tagged as adjective (jj)"dog" is tagged as noun (nn)each word is assigned a tag based on its role in the sentence. for example, "quick" and "brown" are adjectives that describe the noun "fox."workinglet’s see various steps involved in pos tagging:tokenization: the input text is split into individual tokens (words or subwords), this step is necessary for further analysis.preprocessing: the text is cleaned such as converting it to lowercase and removing special characters, to improve accuracy.loading a language model: tools like nltk or spacy use pre-trained language models to understand the grammatical rules of the language, these models have been trained on large datasets.linguistic analysis: the structure of the sentence is analyzed to understand the role of each word in context.pos tagging: each word is assigned a part-of-speech label based on its role in the sentence and the context provided by surrounding words.evaluation: the results are checked for accuracy. if there are any errors or misclassifications, they are corrected.types of pos taggingthere are different types and each has its strengths and use cases. let's see few common methods:1. rule-based taggingrule-based pos tagging assigns pos tags based on predefined grammatical rules. these rules are crafted based on morphological features (like word endings) and syntactic context, making the approach highly interpretable and transparent.example:1. rule: assign the pos tag "noun" to words ending in "-tion" or "-ment".2. sentence: "the presentation highlighted the key achievements of the project's development."3. tagged output:"presentation" → noun (n)"highlighted" → verb (v)"development" → noun (n)2. transformation-based tagging (tbt)tbt refines pos tags through a series of context-based transformations. unlike statistical taggers that rely on probabilities or rule-based taggers, it starts with initial tags and improves them iteratively by applying transformation rules.example:text: "the cat chased the mouse."initial tags: "the" – det, "cat" – noun, "chased" – verb, "the" – det, "mouse" – nounrule applied: change “chased” from verb to nounbecause it follows “the”.updated tags: "chased" becomes noun.3. statistical pos tagging it uses probabilistic models to assign grammatical categories (e.g noun, verb, adjective) to words in a text. unlike rule-based methods which rely on handcrafted rules, it learns patterns from large annotated corpora using machine learning techniques.these models calculate the likelihood of a tag based on a word and its context, helping to resolve ambiguities and handle complex grammar. common models include:hidden markov models (hmms)conditional random fields (crfs)implementing pos tagging with nltklet's see step by step process how pos tagging works with nltk:step 1: installing required resourceshere we import the nltk library and download the necessary datasets using nltk.download().
python

import nltk
from nltk.tokenize import word_tokenize
from nltk import pos_tag
nltk.download('punkt_tab')
nltk.download('averaged_perceptron_tagger_eng')

step 2: applying pos taggingfirst we store the sentence and tokenize it into words using word_tokenize(text). then we apply pos tagging to the tokenized words using pos_tag(words). this assigns a part-of-speech to each word.
python

text = "nltk is a powerful library for natural language processing."
words = word_tokenize(text)

pos_tags = pos_tag(words)

step 3: displaying resultsnow we print the original sentence and loop through the tagged words to show each word with its pos tag.
python

print("original text:")
print(text)

print("\npos tagging result:")
for word, pos_tag in pos_tags:
    print(f"{word}: {pos_tag}")

python

!pip install spacy
!python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm
import spacy
nlp = spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")

step 2: defining and processing the textwe store the sentence in a variable and process it with nlp(text) to get linguistic annotations.
python

text = "spacy is a popular natural language processing library."
doc = nlp(text)

step 3: displaying pos taggingprint the original sentence then loop through the tokens and display each word with its pos tag.
python

print("original text: ", text)
print("pos tagging result:")

def process_text(data):
    data = data.lower()
    # 2. tokenize
    data2 = word_tokenize(data)
    #3. removal of stop words
    nltk_stopwords = set(stopwords.words("english"))
    for w in data2:
        if w in nltk_stopwords:
            count_w = data2.count(w)
            for words in range(count_w):
                data2.remove(w)

    lemm = WordNetLemmatizer()
    data_lemm = [lemm.lemmatize(word) for word in data2]
    text_out = " ".join(data2)
    return text_out

# read each line from the review text and send it to the function to process each line of review
df["Outtext"] = df["reviewText"].apply(process_text)

#now run sentiment analyzer model
analyzer = SentimentIntensityAnalyzer()


# function to read each line and return the intensity value
def get_sentiment(text):
    scores = analyzer.polarity_scores(text)
    sentiment = 1 if scores['pos']>0 else 0
    return sentiment

df['Sentiment']= df['Outtext'].apply(get_sentiment)
